Apex Nourish Corp - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Nourish Corp Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only portions. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Nourish Corp's Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are David Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Ryan Keller, Chief Growth Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Harlan.

David Harlan (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures across commodities and logistics.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: volume and price/mix analysis, market share trends for major brands, performance of key brands and product categories, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, and key achievements and challenges in the quarter.

First, regarding volume and price/mix analysis: Organic net revenue growth came in at 6.2% for the quarter, after adjusting for a 1.1% foreign exchange headwind and a 0.4% impact from divestitures. We broke this down into its core components, achieving a solid 4.1% organic volume growth that more than offset a 2.1% price/mix tailwind. This balanced approach highlights our disciplined execution in a tough environment where shoppers are price-sensitive yet willing to upgrade to premium options.

On volume, the 4.1% organic increase was our strongest since Q4 2021, surpassing the global F&B industry average of 2.3% according to NielsenIQ. Gains stemmed from market share expansion, new product rollouts, and broader distribution. In beverages, which make up 58% of our portfolio, volumes rose 5.2%. Our core carbonated soft drinks like AquaFizz gained 3.8%, thanks to key shelf-space victories over Coca-Cola and PepsiCo in North American club stores, where we added 110 basis points of ACV. Even more impressive, our healthier hydration options, such as plant-based electrolyte drinks under HydroPure and zero-sugar versions, skyrocketed 12.4%, seizing share in the $28 billion functional beverage space driven by wellness demands. This ties directly to our Health-Forward Acceleration program, with 65% of beverage SKUs now under 50 calories per serving—appealing strongly to Gen Z, who favor low-sugar products 2.5 times more than average per IRI insights.

In snacks and nutrition, comprising 42% of revenues, volumes grew 2.7%. Savory lines like ZestCrunch increased 4.1%, boosted by 28% year-over-year e-commerce growth in APAC on platforms like Tmall and Shopee, though value packs felt some strain from inflation-hit consumers in EMEA. Our protein bar expansions, drawing from premium trends like RXBAR, surged 9.2% through partnerships with global gym chains akin to Planet Fitness.

Regionally, performance was strong: North America at 52% of revenues saw +4.8% volumes, with share up 60 basis points to 14.2% via Circana data and convenience store velocity. EMEA, 22% of revenues, posted +3.9%, aided by 7% growth in emerging spots like Poland and Turkey despite UK cost-of-living issues. APAC, 18%, hit +5.6%, spearheaded by +11% in China from ready-to-drink tea growth. Latin America, 8%, managed +2.1% amid FX swings, with Brazil up 4% on localized mango CSD flavors.

For price/mix, the 2.1% contribution fell just shy of our 2.5-3.0% guidance due to ramped-up promotions in developed markets, but net price realization averaged 3.4% after trade spend, moderated by a -1.3% mix shift in sensitive areas. We rolled out 4-6% list price hikes on 80% of North American items in July, securing 85% capture via our company-wide AI dynamic pricing system—similar to Monster Beverage tactics—to counter 7.2% COGS inflation from cocoa and aluminum. Mix faced headwinds from 2% growth in promotional snack multipacks like Family Value bundles, but premium beverages countered with 8.5% mix lift, including 15% from HydroPure RTD coffees as shoppers moved from pricier pods.

These results reinforce our Volume-Led Growth strategy in the Horizon 2025 plan. We've allocated $250 million this year to technical upgrades, like new aseptic lines in Mexico and India for 20% capacity gains, slashing new SKU time-to-shelf to 9 months versus the industry's 12. Our Nielsen partnership and Voyager analytics platform lifted forecast accuracy to 92%, avoiding Q1 stock-outs. Plus, 40% of volume came from sustainable packaging like 100% rPET bottles, meeting EU regs and tripling loyalty among millennials.

Moving forward, we anticipate 3.5-4.5% organic volume growth in Q4, with price/mix at 2.0-2.5% as inflation cools and holidays approach. Share gains targeting 200 basis points over 18 months will come from 50+ launches, including potential CBD wellness drinks post-regulation.

Second, concerning market share trends for major brands: Market share remains central to our strategy in the $1.2 trillion global F&B arena. Using IRI and Nielsen data across 150+ markets for ACV, dollar share, and velocity, we posted 120 basis points of organic gains year-over-year in Q3. While the sector grew 3.2% in constant currency per Kantar, inflation-adjusted volumes were flat at 0.1% amid 4-6% food-at-home inflation. Premium trends shine, with consumers 15% more inclined to premium for health, convenience, and sustainability per our panels. Our mix—beverages 45%, snacks 30%, nutritionals 25%—outpaced category growth 2.1x, lifting total share to 8.4% from 7.9%, our 11th consecutive quarter of gains, beating PepsiCo's 60 bps to 12.1%.

In beverages, CSDs at 14.2% share gained 80 bps sequentially per Circana. Apex Cola hit 22% household penetration, up from 19%, via 12% velocity from Zero Heroes zero-sugar reformulation. Coke leads at 42% but lost 1.1% volume on European sugar taxes; Pepsi held 28% via Gatorade, but we took 0.9 MSP from private labels down to 12%. Non-carb front was stronger: functional waters and RTD teas up 7.8% category-wide, Hydrate+ up 25% sales for 3.2 MSP to 11.5%, topping Red Bull's 9.8% in energy waters via $150 million AI-optimized digital spend for 4:1 ROMI. North America added 150 bps to 18% share with 2,500 Walmart/Kroger doors at 95% ACV; Europe +40 bps to 9.2% despite UK HFSS regs, countered by palm-free certs versus Unilever's 14%.

Snacks share at 16.8% rose 110 bps, topping Mondelez's 21.5% and Kellanova's 13.2%. BFY savory grew 5.1%, Apex Veggie Crisps up 32% volume to 7.4% in plant-based chips with 12g protein and regenerative farming. Chocolate was challenging with Hershey at 36% NA amid 45% cocoa inflation, but our dark premium gained 1.5 MSP, 22% from Amazon/Instacart.

Nutritionals excelled: RTD shakes up 11.2% on GLP-1 trends, NutriPro to 10.1% share (+200 bps) over Premier's 9.5% with clean-label at $2.49, 18% penetration per Numerator. APAC +180 bps to 12% via Tmall D2C; LATAM +20 bps to 8.5% despite FX versus Nestlé's 15%.

By region, North America (55% sales) +140 bps to 11.2% on Costco 98% ACV; EMEA +60 bps to 7.1% with rPET savings $20M; APAC +190 bps to 6.8% on India/Indonesia; LATAM flat at 9.3% but Brazil e-com doubled velocity. Tailwinds: 40% consumers prioritize protein/fiber per Mintel, our 75% BFY portfolio. Headwinds: private labels +2% to 18%, c-store shift to 28% impulse.

Strategically, Precision Nutrition uses ML on 50M loyalty points for 87% accurate personalization via Apex AI app, 22% repeats. $400M BioFuel Snacks buy adds 1 MSP, $50M synergies by FY25. Scope 3 down 18% via supplier pricing, blockchain for 30% cocoa. We eye 100-150 bps FY24 gains to 9.5%, led by beverages 2x category, with $2B pipeline for GLP-1 shakes, upcycled snacks in $250B premium.

Third, in terms of performance of key brands and product categories: Our Nutrition & Snacks segment, 42% of net revenues, grew 6.2% organically, Beverages 4.1%, and Health & Wellness 9.8%. Drivers included volume rebound, pricing amid cocoa/edible oil inflation, and innovation. Crunchy Bites, our savory flagship rivaling Frito-Lay's Lay's and Kettle in the $50B market, hit $1.2B revenues, +8.4% organic on 2% volume and 6.4% pricing. Third straight double-digit NA share gains to 18.2% in tortilla chips via Bold Heatwave flavor, 15% new trial per Nielsen. EMEA softer at 3.1% versus Tyrrells, but 12% A&P hike on TikTok/Spotify for Gen Z. AI dynamic pricing in 500 US doors lifted margins 120 bps.

Zest Beverages, our CSD/energy akin to Pepsi's Mountain Dew/Monster, reached $950M, +5.3% organic: flat volume, 5.3% pricing against 7-9% aluminum/HFCS inflation. Energy up 14.2% on Zest Surge zero-sugar, +220 bps US share to 12.8% in $28B 8% CAGR category. APAC +11% via Tmall/Flipkart D2C bundles at 25% volume. Sustainability: 40% SKUs to rPET, +7% repeats from millennials.

Pure Dairy & Alternatives, like Chobani/Danone, $800M +7.6% organic. Greek yogurts +10% NA volume, Pure Fuel at 14.5% in $10B protein segment on Ozempic trends. Plant-based +2.1% amid trade-down, but SKU cuts focus almond/soy hybrids -20% sugar. Precision fermentation cut costs 8%, margins +150 bps.

Health & Wellness (28% portfolio) $1.1B +9.8% on functional bevs/nutrition bars, premiumization for gut probiotics (11% CAGR to 2030). Convenience foods +3.2%, LatAm volume soft on FX but +7% pricing.

Regions: NA 55% of growth +7.1% on Costco/Sam's; EMEA +1.2% despite HFCS regs, $50M Rotterdam facility; APAC +12.4% Indonesia RTD tea; LatAm +5.8% post-drought.

Vitality Portfolio: accelerate Zest Energy to 20% Beverages FY25, $200M divestitures sugary cereals, $300M R&D for 22 launches (65% velocity in 90 days vs industry). Q4 5-7% growth, holiday/M&A tailwinds in plant-protein.

Fourth, looking at progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: Sustainability anchors our long-term value in F&B, fortifying supply chains, matching consumer shifts, and cutting costs amid regs like EU CSRD and US SEC climate rules.

We're SBTi-aligned, net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2040, full chain by 2050—ahead of Nestlé/Unilever paces. From 2019's 12.5M tCO2e baseline, YTD Q3 cut 22% beating 2025's 20%. Scope 1/2 -18% YoY at 150 facilities via 35% renewable shift to 65% electricity; Texas 100MW solar for 40% NA bev plants, NZ biomass -28% fossils.

Scope 3 (95%) -15% YoY via suppliers: 72% cocoa (150k tons) Rainforest certified + from 55%, Barry Callebaut regen on 200k ha West Africa sequesters 50k tCO2e, +12% yields.

Water intensity -28% to 1.2 L/L product, beating 25% 2025 goal. India replenished 115% via NGOs for 50k farmers, like Danone for 20% APAC sales.

Packaging: virgin plastic -32% to 180k tons, 55% recycled >50% target. rPET 80% EU PET bevs, 100% recyclable for SUPD, $45M savings lightweighting/Veolia.

Regions: NA (45% sales) 25% Green Harvest organic adoption, millennials/Gen Z +10-15% premium per Nielsen. Europe (30%) zero-waste German ops, 98% byproducts to feed. LatAm (15%) 68% RSPO palm. APAC (10%) 45% sourcing, Vietnam coffee 60k holders 4C.

Accretive: Q3 +3% gross margins from $120M avoids, MSCI AA from A, $500M green bonds -50bps. Next: $300M precision ag with John Deere AI sensors on 500k acres for -20% fertilizer, +10% yields. Risks: ISSB Scope 3, El Niño commodities—mitigated by diversification.

We're exceeding goals, leading sustainable F&B for 8-10% CAGR to 2028.

Finally, reviewing key achievements and challenges in the quarter: We posted $2.8B net sales, +9% reported/+11% organic—strongest since post-pandemic. Adjusted EPS $1.42, +12% beating guidance.

Achievements: Volumes accelerated, branded bevs +7% led by +12% functional hydration like VitaQuench vs 5% category; snacks +6% via BetterBite bars +1.5 pts NA savory share vs PepsiCo/Mondelēz. Pricing +4 pts top-line, 6-8% hikes mature sugary bevs, value packs emerging.

APAC stellar +18% to $650M, China +15% oolong RTD in $50B 10% CAGR market. LatAm Brazil guaraná +2 pts vs Ambev, e-com 22% from 15%.

Innovation: HealthForward zero-sugar kombucha 150k cases week 8, pea-protein yogurts -18% costs bioreactor. $50M IBM Watson AI forecast 92%, inventory -12%, $120M capital free.

Sustainability: 40% rPET EU compliant, +8 NPS millennials, Walmart/Tesco space. $85M digitization savings cocoa.

Challenges: Inflation dairy +16%, oils +22%, cocoa +25% Ivory Coast, gross margin -120 bps to 38.5%—offset by pricing/productivity. Legacy CSDs -3% NA vs category -1%, private labels +4 pts. El Niño wheat/disruptions +$40M costs; Europe sugar taxes -2% volume. FX USD strength -3 pts APAC, BRL -50 bps.

Outlook: Premiumization 15% super-premium sales 2025 adaptogens/upcycled; $200M SEA nut milk M&A for plant-based $162B 2030. E-com India/SEA to 30%, NA promotions Fairlife-style. Resilient in 4-6% industry via Agile Innovation, FY organic 8-10%, margins +100 bps.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Patel (CFO):
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $2.8 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year on a reported basis and 6.2% organically. Gross margin was 38.5%, impacted by persistent commodity inflation in areas like cocoa, dairy, and edible oils, though offset by pricing actions and productivity gains. Operating income was $420 million, up 10%, and earnings per share were $1.42. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives like innovation and supply chain resiliency.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, with $300 million authorized remaining under our program.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic growth of 8-10% and adjusted EPS growth of 10-12%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, to ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of commodity inflation on your business?

David Harlan (CEO):
Good question, John. Inflation in key inputs like cocoa up 25% from Ivory Coast yields, dairy 16%, and oils 22% pressured margins by 120 basis points this quarter. We countered effectively with 4-6% pricing across 80% of the portfolio, AI tools for 85% realization, and supply chain efficiencies saving $85 million. This kept us within guidance, and we expect easing in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for new functional beverages and what is the expected impact on growth?

Ryan Keller (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our HealthForward platform launched zero-sugar kombucha with prebiotics and reformulated hydration like VitaQuench, selling 150k cases early. Expect 12-15% category outperformance, adding 1-2 share points in $28B functionals via e-com and club channels, targeting 15% portfolio premium by 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Elena Vasquez (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, disruptions from El Niño wheat and US droughts added $40M, but our $250M investments—new lines in Mexico/India, 92% forecast accuracy via Voyager/IBM—cut inventory 12%, time-to-shelf to 9 months. Regen sourcing for cocoa and rPET shifts build resilience, positioning us for holiday ramps.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Laura Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Lisa Patel (CFO):
Laura, we're on track for FY guidance: 8-10% organic growth, Q4 volumes 3.5-4.5%, price/mix 2-2.5%. Margins expand 100 bps via productivity, innovation tailwinds from 50+ SKUs, and M&A like our nut milk bolt-on. Risks like FX and regs are hedged, with share gains to 9.5%.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to David Harlan for closing remarks.

David Harlan (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Apex Nourish Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
